pr_body:
- PR #13257 fixed a lot of issues but not all and this patch aims to fix almost all remaining issues.
  - the idea in this new patch is to compare position of new glyph with the last position where a glyph has been drawn;
    - no space are "drawn": it just moves the cursor but they aren't added in the chunk;
    - so this way a space followed by a cursor move can be treated as only one space: it helps to merge all spaces into one.
  - to make difference between real spaces and tracking ones, we used a factor of the space width (from the font)
    - it was a pretty good idea in general but it fails with some fonts where space was too big:
    - in Poppler, they're using a factor of the font size: this is an excellent idea (<= 0.1 * fontSize implies tracking space).

Fixes #6705
Fixes #7833
Fixes #9247
Fixes #9998
Fixes #10448
Fixes #10640
Fixes #10900
Fixes #11913
Fixes #13201
Fixes #13226

> Looking at the test results, I do believe that there's too much movement (and some outright regressions) in existing test-cases. The following is a non-exhaustive list (focusing on Firefox), so please go through the test results and see what can be done to improve (some of) these cases:
> 
>     * tracemonkey-text-page1, one case of worse agreement between the canvas/textLayer.

Looking the "Category..." sentence: it looks like a font artifact, because locally chars are almost at the same positions.
Looking at "Copyright...": the 3 chars "ACM" are larger in the pdf than in text layer and everything is shifted.

> 
>     * issue3925-page1, many cases of disagreement between the canvas/textLayer.

Clearly, this one a bit worse...
It's mainly because of:
https://github.com/calixteman/pdf.js/blob/a1add12e187b5dde1e2e8206c47888de80b15bb0/src/core/evaluator.js#L2212
If I decrease it to 0.3 I get almost the same result as before, but at the end the text layer contains more spans.

> 
>     * taro-text-page1..4, worse agreement between the canvas/textLayer for the vertical text.
> 

We must take into account the rotation we've in the current transform.
And when there is a space between two chars (non-spaces) we must add it in 

>     * issue11713-page1, the sizing looks off for the last glyph.

The two final chars with a space between are in the same chunk because of the `MAX_FACTOR`.
It's possible to break the flow when a scale occurs, but I'm not sure that's a good idea to add some code to handle such a corner case.
> 
>     * issue1127-text-page1, there's both improvements and regressions,
> 

It's still a matter of `MAX_FACTOR`.

>     * issue4684-text-page1, lots of separate spaces being inserted.

It's a bug: when a space is between two non-spaces chars and in the same chunk `(xxxSPACExxx) TJ`, we must add a space in the flow.

> 
>     * issue5896-text-page1, another possible issue with space handling (based on the reference images).

It's just a matter of rescale on a span with one space: I'll fix it.

> 
>     * mao-text-page1, slightly worse agreement between the canvas/textLayer in places.
> 

Again because of `MAX_FACTOR`.

>     * issue6605-page1, all spaces seem to be missing in the textLayer (causing bad alignment).

Same issue as for  issue4684-text-page1
/botio test

review_comments: I'm not entirely sure that I understand why the *page* rotation really matters here, since a PDF document can easily specify the current transformation matrix and/or the text matrix such that all text is rendered at an (arbitrary) angle to the page itself?

I added that to handle `issue6019.pdf`: visually we've LTR strings but if we omit the rotation it's TTB (or BTT, I don't remember) strings.
So here I finally just "apply" the rotation matrix to the current text matrix.
It was working ok before my patch because we just got chars from a stream without really thinking about their positions.
Anyway, from a user pov, there are LTR strings.
I finally removed that stuff to handle the rotation we have in the currentTransform.
